chapters.title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A)
chapters.subtitle: Specialist agents, on your site and on others

steps.text: Some jobs are best done by a specialist. This video shows how Agent profiles let your assistants hand work to specialist agents, how your site offers its agents to other systems over the Agent-to-Agent protocol, and how to use the agents of another system.
An assistant that does everything is hard to maintain. Its instructions grow, and its answers become less focused.
A specialist agent has one job, its own instructions and its own tools, so it does that job well.
The Agent-to-Agent protocol, or A2A, lets agents on different systems find each other and work together.
Your site can offer its agents to other systems, and your assistants can call the agents of other systems.

chapters.title: How it is organized
chapters.subtitle: Agents, a host and a client

steps.text: An agent is an AI profile of type Agent, with a description that says what it is good at.
The A2A Host feature offers every Agent profile to other systems, which discover them in the site's agent card.
The A2A Client feature adds connections to the hosts of other systems, and each agent they offer becomes something your assistants can call.
Each part is its own feature, so you only see the menus of the features that are turned on.
Open Artificial Intelligence, Profiles, and click Add Profile. In the New AI Profile window, click Start on Blank profile. The other cards are ready-made profiles, including agents.
Enter a Title, and set the Profile type to Agent. The Description and the Availability appear.
Write the Description for the other assistants. It says exactly what the agent does and when to call it, and it is how they decide.
Availability decides when the agent is included. On demand includes it only when it fits the request. Always available includes it in every request, which uses more tokens.
Under System instructions, tell the agent how to behave. Click Save.
With the Agent-to-Agent Host feature on, your site offers every Agent profile to other systems.
Other systems discover the agents from the site's agent card, and send them messages.
Your technical team chooses how callers sign in: no sign-in for testing, an API key, or OpenID Connect.
When the host asks for it, a caller also needs the Access the A2A Host permission.
To use the agents of another system, open Artificial Intelligence, Agent to Agent Hosts, and click Add Connection.
Enter a Title, and the Endpoint, which is the address of the other system's A2A host. Here the host runs on this machine, and its address ends with slash A2A.
Authentication offers the same choices as an MCP connection: Anonymous, API Key, Basic Authentication, three OAuth 2.0 options, and Custom Headers. Anonymous suits an open host or a test.
Click Save. The site reads the agent card of the host when an assistant first uses the connection.
Open the profile of an assistant, and its Capabilities tab. Under A2A Connections, tick the connection. Each agent that the host offers becomes something the assistant can call.
Under Agents, tick the agents of this site that the assistant may call. Always-available agents are already included.
Click Save.

chapters.title: Ask a specialist
chapters.subtitle: The assistant hands over the job

steps.text: Now ask a question for the specialist: what does the warranty cover?
The assistant hands the question to the Warranty Agent, and answers with what the agent returned.
Specialists: a legal, finance or warranty agent that answers in its own area, with its own instructions.
Partners: a supplier or a sister company offers an agent, and your assistants call it.
Reuse: one agent serves many assistants, so you maintain its instructions in one place.
Care: describe each agent precisely, and give an assistant only the agents it needs.
Create specialist agents, offer them with the A2A Host, and connect to the agents of other systems. Your assistants then hand each job to the right specialist. Thanks for watching.
